description: Believes that subtracting a negative number makes the result smaller, writing a - (-b) as a - b
Believes that the product of two negative numbers is negative
Does not change the sign of a term when moving it to the other side of an equation
correct_rule: A term that moves across the equals sign changes sign: x + a = b gives x = b - a

description: Believes that (-x)^2 is negative, so a squared negative number stays negative
Applies a minus sign in front of a bracket to the first term only
Believes that a negative number divided by a negative number is negative
Gives the sum of a negative and a positive number the sign of the positive number whatever their sizes
correct_rule: The sign of a + b is the sign of the number with the larger absolute value

description: Reverses the order of a subtraction, taking the smaller number from the larger when the smaller comes first
correct_rule: a - b is not b - a

description: Solves -x = c as x = c, ignoring the minus sign on the variable
Multiplies only the first term in a bracket by the number outside
Does not distribute a negative factor over the second term of a bracket
Squares a bracket by multiplying it by 2
Expands a product of two brackets by multiplying only the first terms and the last terms
correct_rule: (a + b)(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd

description: Subtracts a bracket with a coefficient by applying the minus to the first product only
correct_rule: p - a(b + c) = p - ab - ac

description: Multiplies a variable factor by the first term of a bracket only
Multiplies a bracket by a fraction coefficient on the first term only
Loses the minus sign of the second bracket when expanding (x + a)(x - a)
Adds the exponents as well as the coefficients when combining like terms
Combines unlike terms, adding a number and a variable term into one term
correct_rule: Only like terms can be combined

description: Does the operations from left to right, adding before multiplying
Ignores the brackets and multiplies only the nearest number
Combines x and x^2 as like terms
correct_rule: Only terms with the same power of the variable combine

description: Thinks that x * x equals 2x
Reads 3x as 3 + x when substituting a value
Adds the numbers and ignores the signs when combining terms with different signs
Thinks that x + x + x equals x cubed
Adds fractions by adding the numerators and adding the denominators
Subtracts fractions by subtracting the numerators and subtracting the denominators
Divides by a fraction by multiplying by the fraction without turning it upside down
correct_rule: a/b divided by c/d = a/b * d/c

description: Adds a whole number to a fraction by adding it to the numerator only
Multiplies a fraction by a whole number by multiplying both the numerator and the denominator
Simplifies a fraction by subtracting the same number from the numerator and the denominator
correct_rule: Divide the numerator and the denominator by a common factor

description: Reduces (2x)/4 to x/4, dividing only the numerator by 2
Clears the fraction in an equation by multiplying only the fraction term
correct_rule: Multiply every term of the equation by the denominator

description: Writes the reciprocal of a/b with a minus sign
correct_rule: The reciprocal of a/b is b/a

description: Believes that a fraction of a number is found by dividing by the numerator
Believes that (a + b)^2 equals a^2 + b^2
Believes that (a - b)^2 equals a^2 - b^2
Multiplies the base by the exponent instead of using repeated multiplication
correct_rule: x^n is x multiplied by itself n times

description: Adds the exponents when raising a power to a power
Multiplies the exponents when multiplying powers with the same base
Divides the exponents when dividing powers with the same base
Applies a power to the variable only, not to the coefficient, in a product
Believes that a negative exponent makes the number negative
Believes that any number to the power 0 is 0
Reads a power of one half as dividing by 2
Adds the bases as well as the exponents when multiplying powers
Applies an outer exponent to one factor inside a bracket only
Divides only the variable term by its coefficient and leaves the other terms unchanged
correct_rule: Divide every term on both sides

description: Applies an operation to one side of the equation only
correct_rule: Do the same to both sides

description: Subtracts the coefficient instead of dividing by it to isolate the variable
Divides instead of multiplying to undo a division
Subtracts the smaller variable term from the left side only
correct_rule: Subtract the same variable term from both sides

description: Forgets to divide the right-hand side when dividing both sides by the coefficient
Writes the solution of ax = b as x = a/b, inverting the quotient
Drops a variable term from the other side when expanding and collecting
correct_rule: Keep every term of both sides

description: Cross-multiplies a proportion by multiplying the numerators together and the denominators together
Believes an equation that reduces to 0 = 0 has no solution
correct_rule: 0 = 0 is always true, so every number is a solution

description: Gives a solution to a contradiction such as 3 = 4 by setting the variable to 0
Translates 'a number decreased by 4' as 4 - x
Translates 'twice a number plus 3' as 2(x + 3)
Joins the coefficient and the value side by side when substituting
Squares both sides of an equation with a radical by squaring each term on the right separately
Accepts every root found after squaring without checking it in the original equation
correct_rule: Check each root in the original equation
example: sqrt(x + 7) = x - 5: x = 2 or x = 9 -> both are solutions

description: Squares only the variable on the right when squaring both sides
Squares both sides of an equation before isolating the radical
Rejects a root only because it is negative, not because it fails the original equation
correct_rule: Substitute the root into the original equation
example: sqrt(x + 2) = x: x = 2 or x = -1 -> x = -1 is rejected because it is negative

description: Believes that when one root fails the original equation the equation has no solution
correct_rule: Reject only the root that fails
example: x = 2 or x = 9, and 2 fails -> no solution

description: Divides both sides by an expression that contains the variable without considering that it may be zero
Multiplies out the denominators of a rational equation and keeps every root
correct_rule: Reject a root that makes a denominator zero

description: Applies the zero product rule when the product equals a number other than zero
correct_rule: Move everything to one side so that the product is 0

description: Reads the roots of (x - a)(x + b) = 0 with the signs reversed
Solves x^2 = 9 as x = 3 only and loses the negative root
Solves x^2 = 9 by dividing 9 by 2
correct_rule: Take the square root of both sides

description: Gives only the non-zero root of x(x - 5) = 0
Uses b instead of -b in the quadratic formula
Divides only the square root by 2a in the quadratic formula
Completes the square without adding the same number to the other side
correct_rule: Add the same number to both sides

description: Uses b instead of half of b when completing the square
Moves the right-hand side to the left without changing its sign before using the quadratic formula
Swaps the roles of the sum and the product when factorising x^2 + bx + c
correct_rule: The numbers multiply to c and add to b

description: Chooses two numbers that multiply to the constant without checking that they add to the middle coefficient
correct_rule: The numbers must also add to b

description: Ignores the sign of the constant when factorising
Factorises a difference of two squares as a squared bracket
Factorises a sum of two squares as if it were a difference
correct_rule: x^2 + 9 cannot be factorised over the real numbers

description: Takes out a common factor from only some of the terms
correct_rule: Divide every term by the common factor

description: Forgets the 1 that is left when a whole term is the common factor
Gets the sign wrong inside the bracket after taking out a common factor
Factorises ax^2 + bx + c with a not equal to 1 as though a were 1
correct_rule: The leading coefficient changes the factor pairs

description: Believes that sqrt(a + b) equals sqrt(a) + sqrt(b)
correct_rule: sqrt(a + b) cannot be split over a sum

description: Adds the radicands when multiplying square roots
Believes that sqrt(x^2) equals x whatever the sign of x
Gives both signs for a principal square root
Halves the number under the root to take a square root
Rationalises 1/sqrt(a) by multiplying the numerator only
Pulls the wrong factor out of a root when simplifying
Removes a square root from one side of an equation without squaring the other side
Adds the radicands when multiplying numbers with roots
Gives only the positive case when solving an absolute value equation
Drops the sign to give a solution to an absolute value equal to a negative number
Believes that |a + b| always equals |a| + |b|
Changes the sign on the wrong term for the negative case of an absolute value equation
Believes that |-x| equals -x
Removes the absolute value bars without considering the sign of the inside
Does not reverse the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number
correct_rule: Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality

description: Reverses the inequality sign when subtracting from both sides
correct_rule: Only multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses it

description: Treats an inequality as an equation and gives a single value as the answer
correct_rule: The solution of an inequality is a range

description: Solves an absolute value inequality |2x + 1| < 5 as one inequality only
Solves x^2 > 9 as x > 3 and loses the other branch
Writes the solution of x^2 < 9 with 'or' instead of 'and'
Multiplies both sides of an inequality by a variable expression without considering its sign
correct_rule: The direction depends on the sign of the expression

description: Joins the two parts of a compound inequality with 'or'
Cancels a term of the numerator with a term of the denominator
Splits a sum in the denominator into two fractions
Divides only the first term of the numerator when simplifying
correct_rule: Divide every term of the numerator

description: Adds rational expressions by adding the denominators
Believes that x divided by x^2 equals x
Accepts a value that makes a denominator zero as a solution
correct_rule: Exclude values that make a denominator zero

description: Multiplies the denominator but not the numerator when writing a common denominator
correct_rule: Multiply numerator and denominator by the same factor
